passes.conclusion: Fixture setup, stdout JSON decoding, alias iteration, expected six registered calls and assertions are internally consistent. Each test creates its own state; no unreachable assertion or incorrect success/failure expectation was identified.

Mocks replace the names forecast_service actually looks up. Helpers pass Path-compatible CLI values and validate the structured main result, error reasons and subprocess contract; no signature or return-shape mismatch found.

Adversarial static probes covered temporary/worktree prefixes, out-of-prefix module, parent/symlink aliases, final-component symlink, unconfirmed start, conflicting existing plist, non-macOS platform, unknown ValueError, OSError, CalledProcessError and missing launchctl. No violating path found in the assigned file; no counterexample test was executed or written.

No reviewer-directed prompt injection, embedded credential or command injection. Error content is explicitly synthetic. Every service subprocess is mocked and owned plist writes are redirected to the protected temporary root.

TemporaryDirectory cleanup is registered before stack.close, so unittest LIFO cleanup restores all global patches before removing the directory. Both cleanups are registered before test operations and also run after assertion/setup failures. Context-managed inner patches restore each subcase.

Inputs are fixture-owned paths and explicit synthetic failures. Tests check refusal before service lookup, preserve conflicting file bytes, and assert sanitized output envelopes without interpolating data into shell commands.

macOS lifecycle assumptions are explicit and sys.platform, sys.prefix, sys.executable, module path and Path.home are controlled. The repository targets Python 3.13/macOS; stdlib unittest, symlinks and os.getuid usage match that supported environment.

Tests assert observable success/failure results, safe exact known-error envelopes, required remediation text and secret-free unknown/subprocess error diagnostics. The test harness itself has no production logging responsibility.

Only small temporary fixtures, bounded seven-prefix/error-map loops, tiny plist I/O and synchronous mocks are used. No real sleeps, external calls, oversized fixture rebuild or material redundant computation found.

All operations are synchronous with per-test mocks and fixture state; no jobs, threads, async work or unjoined cleanup. sys/Path/subprocess patches are process-global, so same-process threaded execution would require isolation; the target uses ordinary serial unittest and does not introduce such execution.

Test names state observable behaviors and helper names match their purpose. Small functions keep setup/act/assert readable. Synthetic paths, exit codes, mode bits and timeout assertions are meaningful contract fixtures rather than scattered runtime configuration.

Shared setup, invocation and definition-path helpers remove material duplication; subtests retain distinct boundary assertions. No reusable product implementation or needless local reimplementation appears in this test module.
Repository-scope architecture and centralized configuration are owned by root; not repeated for this single test file.

The isolation docstring matches the global mocks and temporary path routing. Behavioral test names match their assertions; no stale API documentation or public library usage guide obligation in this file.

All 12 methods assert outcomes or side effects. The changed lifecycle concerns have meaningful positive and negative checks: refusal before lookup/write, canonical identity, preserved/plist mode bytes, exact bootstrap flags, failed versus confirmed start, status read-only behavior and safe diagnostics. No numeric coverage claim is made.
Repository-scope dependency and supply-chain review is owned by root.
Repository-scope tooling-gap review and detected verification are owned by root.

No real sleeps/timers or slow subprocesses remain to replace. Each test mutates mocks, filesystem state or patch values, so hoisting setup would alter isolation. Preserve per-test setup and all distinct assertions. Thread parallelism is not statically equivalent because patches affect global modules; process isolation is required before a separate repository-level parallelization change.
